question: Israel closes its airspace by September 30?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israel initiates a major closure of its airspace by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or complete suspension of commercial aviation across the entirety of Israeli civilian airspace or a region encompassing a majority of Israeli civilian airspace, including commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from that airspace. A qualifying closure must apply generally to all flights across Israel or a qualifying subset of Israeli airspace. Limited cancellations, delays, temporary ground stops or isolated regional closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain pre-approved flights may be permitted).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, flight suspensions, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Israel will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israeli aviation authorities; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

# Israel airspace closure by Sept 30, 2026: research brief (as of 2026-09-07)

Note: most page fetches failed because the proxy refused the connection. Many facts below come from search-result snippets and could not be checked against the full articles.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria give no URL. The primary source is official information from the Israeli aviation authorities (Civil Aviation Authority, Israel Airports Authority, Transportation Ministry). A consensus of credible reporting can also be used. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/israel-closes-its-airspace-by)
- 2026-09-01: An Octagon page about the market, updated that day, said Israeli airspace "remains operational." [Octagon](https://www.octagonai.co/markets/politics/geopolitics/israel-closes-its-airspace-by)
- I found no official IAA or CAA notice of any closure in September up to 2026-09-07.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. As of early September, Israeli airspace and Ben Gurion airport were open.
- 2026-08-20: A wildcat strike by Ben Gurion staff stopped flights for about an hour, and traffic resumed from 3 p.m. This was a labor action, a temporary ground stop, so it would not count. [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog-august-20-2026/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-05/06: Iran's IRGC fired ballistic missiles at US Navy ships enforcing the US blockade of Iranian ports, including the carrier USS George Washington. CENTCOM said there were no hits. The attacks targeted US ships, not Israel. [ISW/CTP Sept 7](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/iran-update-september-7-2026)
- 2026-09-03: ISW reported that in mid-August Iran warned it would carry out a major strike on Israel if the US moved to seize the Ali al Taher facility. ISW rated a large missile and drone attack on Israel as Iran's "most dangerous" option, but said Iran's degraded long-range missile force may limit it. The same day, Israeli officials said they saw no signs of an imminent Iranian attack on Israel. [ISW/CTP Sept 3](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/iran-update-september-3-2026)
- 2026-09-01: ISW described tit-for-tat strikes between the US and Iran, including Iranian strikes on US bases in Kuwait, the UAE, Jordan and Iraq, and US strikes on Iranian radars. [ISW/CTP Sept 1](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/iran-update-september-1-2026)
- 2026-08-30: The Times of Israel reported staffing worries at Ben Gurion ahead of the Jewish holidays travel peak. [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/airport-meltdown-gives-rise-to-worries-that-ben-gurion-overcrowding-may-be-terminal/)
- 2026-08-17/18: The 60-day US-Iran ceasefire, signed in mid-June, ran out. Trump declined to extend it and said no talks were scheduled. [CNBC Aug 17](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/17/us-iran-war-trump-hormuz.html), [CNBC Aug 18](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/18/us-iran-war-trump-hormuz-trump-ceasefire-expires-extension-.html)
- 2026-07-14: There was a dispute over runway space as US Air Force tankers stationed at Ben Gurion crowded out civilian flights. [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2026/07/14/israeli-tourists-v-us-warplanes-row-over-runway-space-at-ben-gurion-airport/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026-02-28: When the US-Israel war with Iran began, Israel closed its airspace to civilian traffic entirely. [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/lufthansa-ita-airways-resume-flights-to-and-from-ben-gurion-after-iran-war-halt/)
- Around 2026-03-02 onward: A phased reopening began, starting with repatriation flights. [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-okays-plan-to-slowly-reopen-airspace-from-wednesday-night-for-repatriation-flights/amp/), [Octagon](https://www.octagonai.co/markets/politics/geopolitics/israel-closes-its-airspace-by)
- 2026-04-09: After the April 8 ceasefire, Israel lifted all wartime aviation restrictions. [Gulf News](https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/passengers-seen-at-israels-ben-gurion-airport-as-flight-restrictions-lifted-after-iran-truce-1.500501573)
- One aggregator suggested that a Polymarket "by May 8" contract resolved Yes on May 9, 2026. A search snippet also mentioned a temporary closure after a Yemeni missile interception, dated June 8, 2026. I could not verify either, and both may be confused with 2025 events (Houthi missile at Ben Gurion in May 2025; the June 2025 war). [Polyguana](https://polyguana.com/market/2159725), [Yeni Safak](https://en.yenisafak.com/world/israel-closes-airspace-after-intercepting-yemen-missile-amid-iran-tensions-3719216)
- Pattern: in the 2025 and 2026 episodes I could confirm, broad closures came with Israeli or US strikes on Iran, or large Iranian missile attacks on Israel. US-Iran naval clashes in Hormuz since mid-August have not led to a closure.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-09-01: Octagon put the Polymarket September contract at about 6% Yes. [Octagon](https://www.octagonai.co/markets/politics/geopolitics/israel-closes-its-airspace-by)
- 2026-05-06: For comparison, a market analysis cited about 16.5% for a closure by May 31. [Value the Markets](https://value-the-markets-production-butx6j.laravel.cloud/cryptocurrency/news/analyzing-the-impacts-of-israels-military-operations-and-airspace-closure-on-market-dynamics)
- Live Polymarket page: [link](https://polymarket.com/event/israel-closes-its-airspace-by). I could not load it to get a current price, and I found no Kalshi or Manifold equivalent.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The US-Iran naval confrontation and blockade in Hormuz, with no ceasefire in force since August 17. Further escalation could lead to US or Israeli strikes on Iran, or Iranian strikes on Israel.
- Iran's threatened "major strike on Israel" if the US moves on the Ali al Taher facility. [ISW](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/iran-update-september-3-2026)
- The Hezbollah/Lebanon front, which is under a ceasefire that Israel says it is respecting, and possible Houthi missile launches.
- Peak travel over the Jewish High Holidays in September, which raises the cost of any closure decision.
- EASA's Tel Aviv FIR caution bulletins and when US carriers return. Delta had suspended service through Sept 5. Airline decisions by themselves do not count toward resolution. [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/el-al-profit-doubles-as-many-major-foreign-airlines-steer-clear-after-iran-war/)
